findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key credentials are embedded in EC2 user data, placing them in Terraform source/state and making them readable through instance user-data/describe access. Anyone obtaining these credentials can authenticate as the associated IAM principal until they are revoked.

No metadata_options block requires IMDSv2, so the instance can permit IMDSv1. An SSRF flaw on this internet-exposed host could be used to retrieve instance-profile credentials if an instance profile is later attached.

The EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption; absent an account-level default-encryption control, data written to it is stored unencrypted and can be exposed through unauthorized access to underlying storage or snapshots.
This snapshot is created from a volume that is not configured for encryption, so it preserves unencrypted volume data and extends the exposure of that data.
TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing any internet host to attempt SSH authentication and materially increasing brute-force and remote-access attack surface.
The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This gives a compromised web host unrestricted egress for command-and-control and data exfiltration.

The bucket storing VPC Flow Logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Unless an external account-level default encryption control is enforced, log objects may be stored without explicit encryption at rest.
